Kwaru - Hardware & Timber Stock and POS

Hardware and timber yards in Kenya typically run stock, credit and cash on paper and spreadsheets. The first client ran
everything out of an Excel workbook and needed to know what was in each store, who owed what, and how much they made.
Designed, built and deployed Kwaru solo — from first commit to production in under a week, with development continuing since.
FIFO stock batches, transfers between locations, stock takes and adjustments
POS with cash, M-Pesa, bank and cheque, voidable sales, and receipts by SMS or email
credit limits, repayments and running balances
daily figures, profit and loss, and stock value per shop
of the client's existing catalogue, sales history and stock take
— any business can create its own organisation

Spring Boot 4 (Java 25) modular monolith, PostgreSQL 17 with a schema per module, embedded Artemis for
cross-module events

Keycloak with a custom Kwaru theme; realm roles are generated automatically from the API's list of intents,
and role templates (Owner, Manager, Storekeeper, Cashier, Accountant) map onto them
Nuxt 4 static SPA with Nuxt UI, tested with Vitest and Playwright
Apache + systemd on a DigitalOcean droplet; deploys roll back automatically if the new version fails its health check
Live in production and in daily use, with an activity log per organisation recording every change.

Built Art Studios - Portfolio & Lead Generation Site

Mobile-first portfolio and lead-generation site for a Nairobi architecture, interiors and construction studio, built to turn social traffic into qualified enquiries. Features a multi-step project questionnaire with photo uploads, branded share cards generated at build time, a build-failing SEO check, and a Keycloak-protected admin console for leads.

Booking and point-of-sale SaaS for children's hair salons with a parent booking portal. Bookings are held while a deposit is paid, stylist rows are locked to prevent double-booking, and deposit rules handle refunds and forfeits for late cancellations and no-shows. Paystack webhooks are HMAC-verified and idempotent, and provider secrets are encrypted at rest.
